Definition: from G4595; rotten, i.e. worthless (literally or morally):--bad, corrupt. Compare G4190.
BiblicalUsage: The sense of saprós is rotten, that is worthless (literally or morally). In Ephesians 4:29, we read, "…no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth…"; in Luke 6:43, "…good tree bringeth not forth corrupt fruit; neither…". You hear it again in Matthew 7:17 — "Even so every good tree bringeth forth good…" — and in Matthew 7:18, "…good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word saprós is in the Bible for a reason, and it carries weight far beyond its size in the text. I hold that saprós still speaks, because the God who spoke then has not changed.
